authority: Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR)
interpretation: This packet records first-party source observations for reviewer use. It does not approve the authority, opportunity, eligibility rule, benefit, window, or publication status.
sourcePolicy: DSIR and PIB are used as authoritative government evidence. The current Creative India 2025 compendium is treated as programme-context evidence; the legacy PRISM guidelines remain controlling for the specific tracks they cover until DSIR publishes or confirms current operative terms.

records.sourceAnchor: DSIR PRISM page plus Creative India 2025 compendium and PIB launch evidence; current call and successor terms remain to be confirmed
observations: The current DSIR compendium identifies PRISM as Promoting Innovations in Individuals, Start-ups and MSMEs and describes support across idea validation, prototype development, testing/refinement, intellectual property, mentoring and commercialization.

The compendium describes a TOCIC outreach-centre network that provides technical expertise, laboratory/prototyping, testing/validation, mentoring and ecosystem linkages. This is an implementation and support route, not proof that every innovator receives a fixed grant amount.

The current DSIR publications index lists Creative-India-PRISM scheme_2025, published 15 May 2026. The direct compendium is programme-context evidence and contains supported-innovation examples, but it does not establish a universal open application deadline or a single current benefit ceiling.

The PIB release dated 4 January 2026 records the launch of Creative India 2025 under PRISM and the PRISM Network Platform. It confirms programme activity and a current initiative, but it does not replace the operative application guidelines or establish applicant-level entitlement.

The legacy PRISM material separates individual/start-up innovation phases from MSME-cluster R&D proposals. The cluster form and Phase-II guideline should not be merged into one generic grant rule; applicant type, stage, route, eligible cost, matching contribution, review and IP conditions differ by track.

The seed record's earlier window was reported through 30 March 2026. As of this review, a current DSIR call, successor application route, or extension with a universal deadline was not verified, so the opportunity remains closed/review-gated rather than actionable.
reviewFollowUps: Obtain and review the current Creative-India-PRISM scheme document linked from the DSIR publications index, including applicant definitions, phase/category thresholds, eligible costs, benefit ceilings, DBT conditions, milestones, reporting, audit and recovery terms.

Confirm whether DSIR has an active call or notified application route through the DSIR page, TOCIC centres or PRISM Network Platform; do not expose a submit action from the programme compendium alone.

Split the record into separate track-level benefit and eligibility logic for individual innovators/start-ups, Phase-II proposals and MSME-cluster institutional proposals if the current operative documents confirm those routes.
Reconcile the inaccessible or superseded annual-report evidence and the 30 March 2026 window with the current DSIR publication before assigning active, upcoming, closed or superseded status.
Verify the current TOCIC list, local application forms, selection process, IP ownership, DBT/payment conditions, milestone reporting and recovery/clawback terms.

publicationGuard.reason: Current DSIR evidence confirms an active PRISM programme context and the Creative India 2025 initiative, but it does not by itself establish a universal open call, current applicant-level benefit ceiling or operative track-specific terms. Publication requires human reconciliation of the current scheme document, call route and legacy-guideline boundaries.
